title: SLF–FST: a framework for stress-testing fairness under progressive label bias
venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
abstract: Abstract Machine learning models are susceptible to reproducing and amplifying structural inequities present in historical data, leading to unjust outcomes in high-stakes domains such as criminal justice, healthcare, employment, and financial services. This paper investigates the relationship between predictive performance and algorithmic fairness in widely used classification methods under systematically increased, group-conditional bias in training labels. We introduce Systematic Label Flipping for Fairness Stress Testing (SLF–FST), a reproducible evaluation framework that injects controllable bias into training data and tracks the joint evolution of accuracy and group-based fairness metrics as bias intensity increases. Using Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and feedforward Neural Network classifiers, we assess robustness across standard benchmark datasets. Our results reveal comparable degradation trends across classifiers; however, Logistic Regression exhibits the most pronounced decline in both predictive accuracy and fairness on the COMPAS dataset, whereas Random Forests, as an ensemble method, demonstrate the greatest robustness to injected bias. Neural Networks and Decision Trees showed intermediate behavior. These findings suggest that SLF–FST can function as a practical pre-deployment auditing mechanism, enabling practitioners to identify failure thresholds and quantify trade-offs between fairness and predictive performance in risk-sensitive systems.

claims.text: Across evaluated datasets, the LOW label-flipping strategy produces an average cumulative change of -0.058 ± 0.028 in Matthews Correlation Coefficient from pollution rate ρ = 0.00 to ρ = 0.20.
Across evaluated datasets, the LOW label-flipping strategy produces an average cumulative change of 0.292 ± 0.06 in Equalized Odds from pollution rate ρ = 0.00 to ρ = 0.20.
Across evaluated datasets, the HIGH label-flipping strategy produces an average cumulative change of -0.164 ± 0.026 in Matthews Correlation Coefficient from pollution rate ρ = 0.00 to ρ = 0.20.
Across evaluated datasets, the HIGH label-flipping strategy produces an average cumulative change of 0.146 ± 0.056 in Equalized Odds from pollution rate ρ = 0.00 to ρ = 0.20.
Across evaluated datasets, the RANDOM label-flipping strategy produces an average cumulative change of -0.032 ± 0.02 in Matthews Correlation Coefficient from pollution rate ρ = 0.00 to ρ = 0.20.
Across evaluated datasets, the RANDOM label-flipping strategy produces an average cumulative change of 0.208 ± 0.037 in Equalized Odds from pollution rate ρ = 0.00 to ρ = 0.20.
The SLF-FST protocol relabels selected protected-positive instances as negative.
The SLF-FST protocol relabels selected privileged-negative instances as positive.

limitations.text: The confidence-guided LOW and HIGH strategies depend on the auxiliary estimator used to rank eligible instances, and the paper does not include an auxiliary-estimator ablation study.
The empirical evaluation is restricted to comparisons among internal selection strategies and does not include external generic label-noise or data-poisoning baselines.
Each dataset is evaluated using a single binary sensitive attribute without modeling user bias or intersectional relationships among multiple attributes.
Prior genetic-algorithm-based bias generation approaches exhibit scalability limitations on large or high-dimensional datasets.

future_work.text: Extending fairness stress testing methodologies to multi-class classification tasks.
Evaluating calibrated and uncalibrated estimates, alternative auxiliary ranking models, and selection-overlap measures.
Conducting empirical benchmarks that compare SLF-FST with external generic label-noise and data-poisoning techniques under harmonized protocols.
Integrating fairness mitigation algorithms into the stress-testing pipeline and evaluating models in dynamic or evolving data environments.

methodologies.name: Systematic Label Flipping for Fairness Stress Testing (SLF–FST)
methodologies.description: A diagnostic stress-testing framework that perturbs group-conditional training labels across progressive pollution rates to evaluate classifier accuracy and fairness degradation.
conditions: Three selection rules: LOW, HIGH, RANDOM
Auxiliary Random Forest estimator for instance confidence scoring
Four classifier families: Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, feedforward Neural Network
Hyperparameter optimization using Optuna Tree-structured Parzen Estimator over 50 trials targeting validation MCC
